items.en: Unpredictable Arising Across the Four Cultivations
items.zh: 正料揀事理兩修發禪不定
parent: Distinguishing That Dhyāna's Arising Is Not Fixed

zh: 第一、先料揀事理兩修，發禪不定者。問曰：上所明三止，若係緣、制心，此二止並是事止，應但發事中禪定，唯體真一止，既是理止，應發理中禪定，今何故三止通皆發事理諸禪？此則因果渾而無別。答曰：不然。今一家所明事理兩修，悉隨行人根緣，是以發法不同，寧可定有分別？如上所明三止，若略說，則應如所問，合為事、理兩修；若具足分別，應開為四修。就四修中，則有二種：一、約止門明四修；二、約觀門明四修。
en: First, distinguishing beforehand that the arising of dhyāna through both phenomenal and principle cultivation is not fixed. Question: as clarified above, of the three kinds of stopping, fixed-object stopping and restraining-the-mind stopping are both phenomenal stopping, and so should bring forth only phenomenal dhyāna-concentration; embodying-truth stopping alone, being principle stopping, should bring forth only dhyāna-concentration of principle. Why, then, do all three kinds of stopping bring forth both phenomenal and principle dhyānas alike? This would seem to blur cause and effect together with no distinction left between them. Answer: this does not follow. What this school clarifies as phenomenal and principle cultivation follows entirely the practitioner's own capacity and conditions, and so the dharmas brought forth differ accordingly — how could there possibly be any fixed distinction? As clarified above, the three kinds of stopping, if spoken of briefly, would indeed combine as the question suggests into phenomenal and principle cultivation alone; but if distinguished in full, they should instead open into four cultivations. Within these four cultivations, there are two approaches: distinguishing the four cultivations with reference to the gate of stopping; and distinguishing the four cultivations with reference to the gate of contemplation.

zh: 第一、約止門明四修者：一、事止，所謂係緣、制心等止，即是事修；二、理止，所謂體真止，即是理修；三、事理止，所謂緣俗體真止，即是事理修；四、非事非理止，所謂息二邊分別止，即是非事非理修。第二、約觀門明四修者：一、事觀，所謂安般、不淨觀等，即是事修；二、理觀，所謂空、無相等觀，即是理修；三、事理觀，所謂雙觀二諦，即是事理修；四、非事非理觀，所謂中道正觀，即是非事非理修。
en: First, distinguishing the four cultivations with reference to the gate of stopping: phenomenal stopping, namely fixed-object and restraining-the-mind stopping, is precisely phenomenal cultivation; principle stopping, namely embodying-truth stopping, is precisely principle cultivation; phenomenal-and-principle stopping, namely stopping that takes the conventional as its object while still embodying truth, is precisely phenomenal-and-principle cultivation; and neither-phenomenal-nor-principle stopping, namely the stopping that sets to rest the distinguishing of both extremes, is precisely neither-phenomenal-nor-principle cultivation.

Second, distinguishing the four cultivations with reference to the gate of contemplation: phenomenal contemplation, namely mindfulness of the breath, the contemplation of impurity, and the like, is precisely phenomenal cultivation; principle contemplation, namely the contemplations of emptiness, signlessness, and the like, is precisely principle cultivation; phenomenal-and-principle contemplation, namely the paired contemplation of the two truths, is precisely phenomenal-and-principle cultivation; and neither-phenomenal-nor-principle contemplation, namely the correct contemplation of the middle way, is precisely neither-phenomenal-nor-principle cultivation.

zh: 今為欲成前止門發禪不定義故，但約四止以明修，一一修中各有四種發禪不定，是故四種修中合有十六種發禪不定。行者善識此相，即自了知事理兩修通發一切諸禪三昧，心無疑惑。云何名為四種止中，一一各有四種發禪不定？
en: Here, in order to establish the point that dhyāna's arising through the gate of stopping is not fixed, only the four kinds of stopping are used to clarify cultivation: within each of these four cultivations there are, in turn, four kinds of unpredictable arising, so that the four cultivations together give sixteen kinds of unpredictable dhyāna-arising in all. Once the practitioner has properly recognized this pattern, one comes to understand of oneself that phenomenal and principle cultivation alike bring forth every dhyāna-samādhi in common, and the mind is left with no doubt about it. What, then, is meant by saying that each of the four kinds of stopping has, in turn, four kinds of unpredictable arising?

zh: 今先料揀第一、事修發禪不定，即有四種不同：一、自有行人安心係緣、制心等事止，還發事中禪定，謂根本四禪、四無量心、四無色定及九想、背捨、勝處、一切處等中諸禪三昧。二、自有行人安心事止，而但發理中禪定，謂空、無相、無作、三十七品、四諦、十二因緣等慧行理中諸禪三昧。三、自有行人安心事止，具發事理禪定，謂根本四禪、四無量心、四無色定、九想、背捨、勝處、一切處等事中諸禪三昧，空、無相、無作、三十七品、四諦、十二因緣等慧行理中諸禪三昧，乃至特勝、通明皆屬事理禪定。四、自有行人安心事止，乃發非事非理禪定，謂自性禪、一切禪等及法華三昧、一行三昧、首楞嚴、師子吼等中道所攝諸禪三昧，乃至十力、無畏、不共之法。
en: Here, first distinguishing the unpredictable arising of dhyāna through phenomenal cultivation: this itself has four differing kinds. First, some practitioners, settling the mind in phenomenal stopping such as fixed-object stopping or restraining-the-mind stopping, bring forth phenomenal dhyāna-concentration in turn — namely the four root dhyānas, the four immeasurable minds, the four formless attainments, and the dhyāna-samādhis among the nine contemplations, the liberations, the stations of mastery, and the totality-bases. Second, some practitioners, settling the mind in phenomenal stopping, bring forth only dhyāna-concentration of principle — namely the wisdom-conduct dhyāna-samādhis of principle among emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the Four Noble Truths, and the twelve links of dependent origination. Third, some practitioners, settling the mind in phenomenal stopping, bring forth both phenomenal and principle dhyāna-concentration together — namely the phenomenal dhyāna-samādhis among the four root dhyānas, the four immeasurable minds, the four formless attainments, the nine contemplations, the liberations, the stations of mastery, and the totality-bases, together with the wisdom-conduct dhyāna-samādhis of principle among emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the Four Noble Truths, and the twelve links of dependent origination — even the special-excellences dhyāna and the thorough-and-bright contemplation both belong to this phenomenal-and-principle dhyāna-concentration. Fourth, some practitioners, settling the mind in phenomenal stopping, bring forth instead neither-phenomenal-nor-principle dhyāna-concentration — namely the samādhi of self-nature, the all-encompassing dhyāna, and the like, the Lotus Samādhi, the samādhi of a single practice, the Śūraṅgama, the lion's roar, and the other middle-way-embracing dhyāna-samādhis, extending even to the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, and the unshared qualities.

zh: 問曰：若修事止，但應發事中禪定，今何得發理及非事理等諸禪三昧不共法耶？答曰：發禪有二種：一者、現前方便修得；二者、發宿世善根。若事修還發事禪者，多是修得。若事修而發理、發非事非理等諸禪三昧者，悉是發宿世禪定善根也。如數人辨有二種修義：一、得修；二、行修。得修，名本所未得。行修，名本已曾得。今此類然，故約事修，則發禪有四種不定。
en: Question: if one cultivates phenomenal stopping, should this not bring forth only phenomenal dhyāna-concentration? How, then, can it bring forth dhyāna-samādhis and unshared dharmas of principle, or of neither phenomenon nor principle? Answer: the arising of dhyāna is of two kinds — attainment through skillful means cultivated in the present; and the arising of wholesome roots from past lives. If phenomenal cultivation brings forth phenomenal dhyāna in turn, this is, for the most part, present attainment through cultivation. But if phenomenal cultivation brings forth dhyāna-samādhis of principle, or of neither phenomenon nor principle, this is, in every case, the arising of dhyāna-concentration's wholesome roots from past lives. As the Ābhidharma masters distinguish, cultivation has two senses: the cultivation of attainment, and the cultivation of exercise. The cultivation of attainment refers to what was not originally attained; the cultivation of exercise refers to what was already attained before. The present case follows this same pattern — hence, with reference to phenomenal cultivation alone, there are four kinds of unpredictable dhyāna-arising.

zh: 復次，今此內方便所明，但辨因止發宿世善根，是故雖說事理諸禪三昧發相，皆略而淺近。若論修習成就，因果相稱，從始至終，諸禪三昧事理廣深之相，並屬第七大段，彼中方復具足分別。
en: Furthermore: what is clarified here, within the internal expedient means, only distinguishes the arising of wholesome roots from past lives through stopping — hence, although the marks of both phenomenal and principle dhyāna-samādhis arising have been described, all of it has been given only in brief and only at a shallow, introductory level. Should one wish to discuss cultivation brought to its own completion, cause matching effect from beginning to end, and the vast, deep marks of every dhyāna-samādhi's phenomenal conduct and underlying principle, this belongs entirely to the seventh great section, where it will at last be distinguished in full.

The question this section opens with is a fair one — if fixed-object and restraining-the-mind stopping are "phenomenal" practices, shouldn't they only ever yield phenomenal results? The treatise's answer turns on a distinction worth holding onto: dhyāna may arise either through skillful means cultivated in the present (修得) or through the resurfacing of a wholesome root from some past life (發宿世善根). Phenomenal cultivation that yields phenomenal dhyāna is mostly the former; when phenomenal cultivation yields a principle-level or "neither" result, that is the latter — a pairing the treatise likens to the Ābhidharma masters' "cultivation of attainment" and "cultivation of exercise," not to the habituation-cause/retribution-cause pair seen earlier in this fascicle. Nor is a strong past cause the only route: the next section adds that, through the skillful means of prajñā-pāramitā, a weak cause with a strong present condition can also bring forth the "neither" level. Together this gives a full account of why practice and outcome so often fail to match — a warning against assuming a student's attainment reveals which technique deserves credit.

quiz.q: In the four cultivations of the gate of stopping, what are phenomenal-and-principle stopping and neither-phenomenal-nor-principle stopping?
options: phenomenal-and-principle: taking the conventional as object while embodying truth; neither: stilling the distinction of both extremes
quiz.why: "Phenomenal-and-principle stopping, namely stopping that takes the conventional as its object while still embodying truth ... neither-phenomenal-nor-principle stopping, namely the stopping that sets to rest the distinguishing of both extremes."

quiz.q: How does the text explain phenomenal cultivation bringing forth principle or neither-phenomenal-nor-principle dhyāna?
options: dhyāna arises either from present cultivation or from past wholesome roots; this case is always past wholesome roots arising
quiz.why: "The arising of dhyāna is of two kinds — attainment through skillful means cultivated in the present; and the arising of wholesome roots from past lives ... if phenomenal cultivation brings forth dhyāna-samādhis of principle, or of neither phenomenon nor principle, this is, in every case, the arising of dhyāna-concentration's wholesome roots from past lives."
